metadata.description: Climate change projections for Wisconsin natural hazards
sources: IPCC AR6 Working Group I Chapter 11 (2021)
Wisconsin Initiative on Climate Change Impacts (WICCI) 2021 Assessment
Great Lakes Integrated Sciences and Assessments (GLISA)
metadata.validation_note: exposure_multiplier values must fall within climate_projection_ranges defined in config/risk_weights.yaml

flood.notes: NOAA/WICCI: 10-20% increase in heavy precipitation events (>2 inches/day) in Great Lakes region by 2050. Wisconsin has seen 37% increase in extreme precipitation since 1950s.

tornado.notes: IPCC AR6: Increasing atmospheric instability may increase severe convective storm environments by 10-15%. Research suggests tornado alley shifting eastward toward Great Lakes. Uncertainty remains high.

winter_storm.notes: NOAA/WICCI: Mixed effects - fewer but more intense winter storms projected. Lake-effect snow may increase 10-20% with warmer Great Lakes water. More ice storms as temperatures oscillate around freezing. Shorter snow season overall.

thunderstorm.notes: EPA/NOAA: 15-30% increase in severe thunderstorm environments projected by 2050. Warmer atmosphere holds more moisture, increasing severe weather energy. Derecho and straight-line wind events may increase significantly.

straight_line_wind.notes: EPA/NOAA: 15-30% increase in severe convective wind environments by 2050; derecho frequency and intensity projected to rise across the upper-Midwest corridor (Brooks et al., NOAA SPC; EPA Climate Indicators). Warmer, moister atmosphere amplifies downburst potential.

wisconsin_thunderstorm_severity.description: County-level severe thunderstorm severity index based on NOAA Storm Events Database historical patterns, NWS warning frequencies, and geographic factors. Scale 0-1.
wisconsin_thunderstorm_severity.data_source: NOAA Storm Events Database (2010-2024), NWS severe thunderstorm warnings
wisconsin_thunderstorm_severity.methodology: County-level events per year divided by 95th percentile events/year across all 72 WI counties, clipped to [0.15, 0.85] range.
wisconsin_thunderstorm_severity.source: NOAA NCEI Storm Events Database, 2006-2025 (20-year aggregation). Severity score = county thunderstorm events per year (Thunderstorm Wind + Hail + Lightning + Funnel Cloud), normalized to 0.15-0.85 using Wisconsin 95th percentile as ceiling.
